question: What is a transfer income?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Unearned income**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Transfer income** refers to income received without providing any goods or services in return.
 
• This type of income typically includes **welfare payments, social security benefits, and other government subsidies**.
 
• It is termed **unearned income** as it is not earned through active employment or business activities.
 
• Examples include **pensions, unemployment benefits, and child support payments**.
 
• Transfer incomes are primarily aimed at **supporting individuals and households** in financial need.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Earned Income**: Income derived from active work such as salaries, wages, and business profits.
 
• **Disposable Income**: The amount of money left to spend or save after taxes have been deducted from earnings.
 
• **Public Income**: Revenue collected by the government from various sources like taxes, fees, and public enterprises.
 
• **Unearned Income**: Includes transfer incomes, interest, dividends, and other forms of income not resulting from labor or business activities.
 
• Transfer payments are a significant part of **fiscal policy**, used to redistribute wealth and provide financial stability to vulnerable populations.
